holidays.name: Cinco de Mayo
holidays.description: A celebration of Mexican heritage and culture that in the United States has turned into a giant festival of tacos, margaritas, sombreros, and mariachi music.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the Mexican army's unlikely victory over French forces at the Battle of Puebla on May 5, 1862. Mexican-Americans in California embraced the date in the 1860s as a show of solidarity with Mexico.
holidays.funFact: Cinco de Mayo is not Mexico's Independence Day (that's September 16), and it is celebrated far more enthusiastically in the U.S. than in most of Mexico, where it is mainly observed in the state of Puebla.

holidays.name: Revenge of the Fifth
holidays.description: A playful Star Wars fan holiday for Sith lords and dark side devotees, the villainous answer to May the Fourth, when fans trade Jedi robes for Imperial capes and heavy breathing.
holidays.origin: The name riffs on the 2005 film Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith (originally pitched as 'Revenge of the Jedi' for the 1983 film). Fans started marking May 5 as the day after Star Wars Day to give the dark side its due.
holidays.funFact: George Lucas originally titled Return of the Jedi as 'Revenge of the Jedi' and even printed posters and T-shirts before deciding that Jedi wouldn't seek revenge, which is a Sith trait.

holidays.name: National Hoagie Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the mighty submarine sandwich, piled with deli meats, cheese, crisp veggies, and oil and vinegar, all stuffed into a long roll.
holidays.origin: The hoagie is a Philadelphia specialty. One popular origin story says it came from Italian workers at the Hog Island shipyard during World War I, who were called 'hoggies' and ate big sandwiches for lunch.
holidays.funFact: In 1992, Philadelphia's Pennsylvania state legislature-adjacent hoagie fans were so serious about the sandwich that the city has long argued over whether it is a hoagie, a sub, a hero, or a grinder depending on where you stand.

holidays.name: International Midwives' Day
holidays.description: A worldwide day of appreciation for the midwives who help bring new humans into the world, often with remarkable skill, patience, and very little sleep.
holidays.origin: The day was first proposed in 1987 at a conference of the International Confederation of Midwives in the Netherlands and has been observed every May 5 since 1992.
holidays.funFact: Midwifery is considered one of the oldest professions in human history, and references to midwives appear in ancient Egyptian texts, including the Ebers Papyrus from around 1550 BCE.

holidays.name: Children's Day in Japan (Kodomo no Hi)
holidays.description: A national holiday in Japan where families fly colorful carp-shaped streamers called koinobori, display samurai helmets, and eat sticky rice cakes wrapped in leaves to wish children health and strength.
holidays.origin: It began as Tango no Sekku, a seasonal festival with roots in ancient China, and became an official national holiday in Japan in 1948 as part of Golden Week.
holidays.funFact: The carp streamers are used because carp are said to swim bravely upstream and turn into dragons, so each fish stands for a child's hope of overcoming obstacles.
